questions.prompt: Find the first three terms of (1−x/5)^(1/2) in ascending powers of x, and state the strict interval of validity. [4 marks]
markPoints: Write (1−x/5)^(1/2) using (1+u)ⁿ with n=1/2 and u=−x/5.
The constant term is 1 and the linear term is (1/2)(−x/5)=−x/10.
questions.modelAnswer: Write (1−x/5)^(1/2) using (1+u)ⁿ with n=1/2 and u=−x/5. The constant term is 1 and the linear term is (1/2)(−x/5)=−x/10. The quadratic term is (1/2)(−1/2)(x²/25)/2=−x²/200. Hence (1−x/5)^(1/2)≈1−x/10−x²/200 for |x|<5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Pure practice linked to AQA June 2022 Paper 3 general methods
questions.prompt: The graphs y=2x and y=x² meet at x=0 and x=2. Find the exact area enclosed between them, explaining which curve is uppermost. [5 marks]
markPoints: On 0<x<2, 2x exceeds x², so the line is the upper graph.
The exact enclosed area is 4/3 square units.
questions.modelAnswer: On 0<x<2, 2x exceeds x², so the line is the upper graph. The enclosed area is ∫₀²(2x−x²)dx. Integrate to obtain [x²−x³/3]₀². Substitute the limits to give 4−8/3. The exact enclosed area is 4/3 square units.

questions.series: Original Pure practice linked to AQA June 2022 Paper 3 general methods
questions.prompt: For the function f(x)=3x−4, find f⁻¹(x) and solve exactly f(x)=f⁻¹(x). [4 marks]
markPoints: Write y=3x−4 and interchange x and y.
Multiply through to obtain 9x−12=x+4, so x=2.
questions.modelAnswer: Write y=3x−4 and interchange x and y. Rearrange x=3y−4 to get f⁻¹(x)=(x+4)/3. Equate the expressions: 3x−4=(x+4)/3. Multiply through to obtain 9x−12=x+4, so x=2.

questions.prompt: Find the indefinite integral of 3√x+4/x² with respect to x, simplifying the result and including the integration constant. [3 marks]
questions.modelAnswer: Rewrite the integrand as 3x^(1/2)+4x^(−2). Use ∫xⁿdx=x^(n+1)/(n+1)+C for n≠−1. The result is 2x^(3/2)−4/x+C.

questions.series: Original Pure practice linked to AQA June 2022 Paper 3 general methods
questions.prompt: For 0≤x<2π, consider y=2sin(3x). State its amplitude and period, then solve the equation 2sin(3x)=1 exactly and give the number of solutions. [5 marks]
markPoints: The amplitude is 2 and the period is 2π/3.
For k=0,1,2 there are exactly six solutions in 0≤x<2π.
questions.modelAnswer: The amplitude is 2 and the period is 2π/3. The equation simplifies to sin(3x)=1/2. For one turn, 3x=π/6 or 5π/6 modulo 2π. Thus x=π/18+2kπ/3 or x=5π/18+2kπ/3. For k=0,1,2 there are exactly six solutions in 0≤x<2π.

questions.prompt: A curve is defined by x=t³−3t and y=t²+1. Find dy/dx for t≠±1, and determine the tangent at t=2. [5 marks]
markPoints: Differentiate the parametric equations to get dx/dt=3t²−3.
At t=2 the point is (2,5) and the gradient is 4/9.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate the parametric equations to get dx/dt=3t²−3. Differentiate y to obtain dy/dt=2t. Therefore dy/dx=(2t)/(3t²−3), where dx/dt≠0. At t=2 the point is (2,5) and the gradient is 4/9. The tangent is y−5=(4/9)(x−2).

questions.prompt: For y=Abˣ with A>0 and b>0, a straight-line graph has equation log₁₀y=0.2x+1.3. Find A, b, y at x=2, and the percentage increase per unit x. [5 marks]
markPoints: The percentage increase per unit x is 100(b−1)≈58.5%.
questions.modelAnswer: Taking logs gives log₁₀y=log₁₀A+xlog₁₀b. The intercept implies A=10^1.3. The gradient implies b=10^0.2≈1.5849. At x=2, log₁₀y=1.7, hence y=10^1.7≈50.12. The percentage increase per unit x is 100(b−1)≈58.5%.

questions.prompt: Differentiate y=(x²+1)⁴. Find its stationary point and use the second derivative at that point to classify it. [4 marks]
markPoints: Thus dy/dx=8x(x²+1)³, which is zero only when x=0.
Differentiating the gradient and setting x=0 gives y″(0)=8>0, so it is a local minimum.
questions.modelAnswer: Apply the chain rule: dy/dx=4(x²+1)³(2x). Thus dy/dx=8x(x²+1)³, which is zero only when x=0. The stationary point is (0,1). Differentiating the gradient and setting x=0 gives y″(0)=8>0, so it is a local minimum.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Pure practice linked to AQA June 2022 Paper 3 general methods
questions.prompt: Prove by contradiction that if the square of an integer n is odd, then n is odd. [4 marks]
markPoints: Assume n² is odd but n is even.
Then n=2k for some integer k.
This contradicts n² being odd; therefore n must be odd.
questions.modelAnswer: Assume n² is odd but n is even. Then n=2k for some integer k. So n²=4k²=2(2k²), which is even. This contradicts n² being odd; therefore n must be odd.

questions.series: Original Pure practice linked to AQA June 2022 Paper 3 general methods
questions.prompt: For f(x)=x³−6x²+9x+2, find both stationary points and classify them. For which values of k does f(x)=k have three distinct real solutions? [7 marks]
markPoints: Factorise as f′(x)=3(x−1)(x−3), giving x=1 or x=3.
Since f″(1)=−6<0, (1,6) is a local maximum.
Since f″(3)=6>0, (3,2) is a local minimum.
Horizontal levels strictly between 2 and 6 cut all three branches, so 2<k<6.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate to get f′(x)=3x²−12x+9. Factorise as f′(x)=3(x−1)(x−3), giving x=1 or x=3. The stationary points are (1,6) and (3,2). The second derivative is f″(x)=6x−12. Since f″(1)=−6<0, (1,6) is a local maximum. Since f″(3)=6>0, (3,2) is a local minimum. Horizontal levels strictly between 2 and 6 cut all three branches, so 2<k<6.
